(Louisville, Kentucky) | college = [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] (2019–2021) | highlights = }} '''David Johnson''' (born February 26, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]]. ==Early life and high school career== Johnson grew up in [[Louisville, Kentucky]] and attended [[Trinity High School (Louisville)|Trinity High School]]. As a sophomore, Johnson averaged 10.5 points and 4.8 rebounds per game and was named third team All-State.{{cite web|last=Kareell|first=David|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2017/05/25/trinitys-david-johnson-called-into-usa-basketball-under-16-training-camp/346084001/|title=Trinity's David Johnson called into USA Basketball Under-16 training camp|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=May 25, 2017|accessdate=March 17, 2020}} He was named first team All-State as a junior after averaging 13.9 points, 5.8 rebounds and 5.2 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2018/04/13/kentucky-boys-basketball-all-state-trinitys-david-johnson/513514002/|title=Kentucky boys basketball All-State: Trinity's David Johnson|first=Jason|last=Frakes|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=April 13, 2018|access-date=March 17, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2018/11/16/stronger-david-johnson-looking-lead-trinity-and-mr-basketball-race/1977487002/|title=Stronger David Johnson looking to lead Trinity and Mr Basketball race|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=November 16, 2018|access-date=March 17, 2020}} Johnson was ranked a four-star recruit and the best college prospect in the state of Kentucky by [[ESPN]] and committed to play at Louisville early during his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Four-star-guard-David-Johnson-commits-to-Louisville-122293724/|title=Four-star guard David Johnson commits to Louisville|first=Evan|last=Daniels|website=247Sports.com|date=September 22, 2018|access-date=March 17, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://theathletic.com/1025842/2019/06/19/a-look-at-louisville-bound-guard-david-johnson/|title=A look at Louisville-bound guard David Johnson |first=Jeff|last=Greer|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=June 19, 2019|access-date=March 17, 2020}} He de-committed after Louisville was named as part of the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal]], but recommitted after considering offers from Georgia and Xavier.{{cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/trinity-basketball-star-david-johnson-commits-to-hometown-louisville-again|title=Trinity basketball star David Johnson commits to hometown Louisville — again|first=Danielle|last=Lerner|website=USATodayHSS.com|date=September 23, 2018|access-date=March 17, 2020}} in the As a senior, Johnson averaged 16.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and four assists per game and was named First Team All-State and the Player of the Year by the ''[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]''. He was named the MVP of the Kentucky Sweet 16 state tournament after recording 22 points, 12 rebounds, two assists and four blocked shots in the state title game.{{cite web|url=https://www.wdrb.com/sports/louisville-freshman-david-johnson-injures-shoulder-could-be-out-/article_2c14972e-aef1-11e9-8152-7b0f024e5518.html|title=Louisville freshman David Johnson injures shoulder, could be out 4-6 months|first=Eric|last=Crawford|website=WDRB.com|date=July 25, 2019|access-date=March 17, 2020}} He scored 1,472 points and grabbed 719 rebounds in four seasons as a starter at Trinity.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/louisville/Article/louisville-mens-basketball-david-johnson-chris-mack-trinity-high-school-georgia-tech-142476365/|title=Louisville freshman David Johnson not expected to miss any time|first=Jody|last=Demling|website=247Sports.com|date=January 20, 2020|access-date=March 17, 2020}} ==College career== Johnson missed the beginning of his freshman season with an offseason shoulder injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/louisville/basketball/ulmbb-johnson-progressions|title=David Johnson continues to progress for Louisville backcourt|first=Sam|last=Draut|website=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]|date=January 17, 2020|accessdate=March 17, 2020}} Johnson played mostly as a key reserve during his freshman season with occasional starts. He scored a season high 19 points with seven assists, four rebounds and three steals in Louisville's upset win over [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] on January 18, 2020.{{cite web|url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/01/18/david-johnson-shines-as-no-11-louisville-beats-no-3-duke-79-73/|title=David Johnson shines as No. 11 Louisville beats No. 3 Duke, 79-73|first=Rob|last=Dauster|website=[[NBC Sports]]|date=January 18, 2020|accessdate=March 17, 2020}} Johnson started at point guard against [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] on February 19, 2020 and led the team with seven assists in the 90–66 win in addition to three points.{{cite web|url=https://www.wdrb.com/sports/bozich-for-starters-david-johnson-leads-louisville-past-syracuse/article_aae2fa40-539d-11ea-b62d-8fc02a921540.html|title=For starters, David Johnson leads Louisville past Syracuse|first=Rich|last=Bozich|website=WDRB.com|date=February 19, 2020|accessdate=March 17, 2020}} Johnson averaged 6.3 points, 2.8 assists and 2.8 rebounds per game in 27 games with four starts for the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2020/03/10/louisville-basketball-david-johnson-could-key-postseason-run/4824527002/|title=Louisville basketball: David Johnson could be key to postseason run|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=March 10, 2020|accessdate=March 17, 2020}} As a sophomore, he averaged 12.6 points, 3.2 assists and 5.8 rebounds per game. Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Bozich |first1=Rick |title=David Johnson leaving Louisville basketball for 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://www.wdrb.com/sports/david-johnson-leaving-louisville-basketball-for-2021-nba-draft/article_c8ed4cbc-9d38-11eb-b36a-9bc29881a814.html |access-date=June 24, 2021 |work=WDRB |date=April 14,
